correctness.rationale: The square-zero power expansion proves \(X_B^{2r}=0\) and \(X_B^{2r-1}=\varepsilon A^{r-1}BA^{r-1}\). Therefore maximal index is equivalent to a nonzero highest-power sandwich. The failure locus is the kernel of a linear operator of rank \(s^2\), since vectorization represents it by \((A^{r-1})^T\otimes A^{r-1}\). The finite-field count follows from kernel dimension. The argument includes \(A=0\), and exhaustive finite checks reproduce the criterion and counts.

originality.rationale: The closest recent primary result gives only the universal doubled-index upper bound, while the closest published exact count treats a single Jordan block. The new statement identifies the maximal-index locus for every nilpotent real part and derives its codimension and finite-field density from the rank of the highest-power sandwich map. Searches in published-finding corpus and the public literature found no equivalent arbitrary-Jordan-type formula.
residual_risks: Older literature on square-zero extensions or first-order matrix perturbations may encode the same maximal-lift count under different terminology despite the targeted searches.

value.rationale: The claim fills the explicit multi-block gap left by the closest exact one-block result at the structurally important maximal-index boundary. It identifies a similarity-invariant control parameter, the number \(s\) of largest Jordan blocks, and turns it into an exact codimension and probability. This is more informative than a routine example or parameter increment and gives a reusable criterion for arbitrary nilpotent standard parts.
